parts.problem_md:
![Diagram of a right-angled triangle with a base of 3.2 m, a hypotenuse of 6.9 m. "NOT TO SCALE" is written on the right side.](assets/001-diagram-of-a-right-angled-triangle-with-a-base-o.png)

A vertical flagpole is set on horizontal ground.
A guy rope of length 6.9 metres is attached to the top of the flagpole, and is also fixed to the ground 3.2 metres from the bottom of the flagpole.

Calculate the height of the flagpole.

............................................ m
parts.solution_md:
The flagpole, the ground, and the guy rope form a right-angled triangle

- so you can use Pythagoras' theorem

Use the Pythagoras formula $a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$

- with $a=3.2$ and $c=6.9$

  - Remember that $c$ must be the hypotenuse (longest side) of the triangle
- Then $b$ will be the height of the flagpole

$3.2^{2}+b^{2}=6.9^{2}$

**[M1]**

Subtract $3.2^{2}$ from both sides, to get $b^{2}$ on its own

$b^{2}=6.9^{2}-3.2^{2}$

**[M1]**

Take the square root of both sides

- This will get rid of the 'squared' on the left-hand side

$b=\sqrt{6.9^{2}-3.2^{2}}$

- Use your calculator to work out that value

$b=6.113100...$

Round to a suitable degree of accuracy

- In general you should round to 3 significant figures, unless the question specifies otherwise
- The fourth significant figure is a '3'

  - which tells you not to change the third significant figure '1'

**Final answer:** **6.11 m (3 s.f.)**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For `3.2 squared plus open square brackets... close square brackets squared equals 6.9 squared` or equivalent.
> 
> **M1**: For $6.9^{2}-3.2^{2}$ or equivalent. Earning this mark automatically earns the previous 'M' mark.
> 
> **A1**: For 6.1[1] or 6.113... .

![Rectangle ABCD with side AB 12 cm, diagonal AC 15 cm, and vertices labelled A, B, C, D. Diagonal is dashed.](assets/002-rectangle-abcd-with-side-ab-12-cm-diagonal-ac-15.png)

The diagram shows a rectangular piece of wood $ABCD$.

$AB=$ 12 cm and $AC=$ 15 cm.

Calculate $BC$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Using Pythagoras' Theorem *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$

- $a=AB=12$
- $b=BC$
- $c=AC=15$

$12^{2}+b^{2}=15^{2}\,144+b^{2}=225$

**[M1]**

> *Rearrange for **b*

`table row cell b squared end cell equals cell 225 minus 144 end cell row cell b squared end cell equals 81 end table`

> *Square root*

$b=\sqrt{81}\,b=9$

**[M1]**

$BC=9\mathrm{cm}$

**[A1]**

![q9-058031-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/005-q9-058031-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

The diagram shows a field in the shape of a trapezium. $AB=150m,BC=90m$ and $CD=120m$. 
Angle $ABC$ = angle $BCD$ = $90^{\circ}$.

i) Show that $AD=95m$, correct to the nearest metre.

[3]

ii)A fence is built around the perimeter of the field.

It costs `$ 48` to build each 5-metre section of the fence. Calculate the cost of building this fence.

`$` .................................... [3]
parts.solution_md:
(i)*Draw a triangle **ADX **as shown below* *DX **will be 90 m as it is the same as **CB* *AX **will be 30 m as it is the difference between **DC** and **AB*

![pythagoras-h-3-1](assets/006-pythagoras-h-3-1.png)

> *Apply Pythagoras to the triangle **AXD **to find length **AD*

$AD=\sqrt{30^{2}+90^{2}}=94.86832981...m$

**Method ****[2]**

**Unrounded answer**** [1]**

> *Round to the nearest metre*

**95 m** *This is a "show that" question, so full working needs to be shown  *

(ii) *Find the total perimeter (distance around the edge)* *Use the 95 m value for the length of **AD*

*120 + 90 + 150 + 95 = 455 m*

**[1]**

*It costs \$48 per 5 metres* *So find how many 5 metres are in 455 m*

*455 ÷ 5 = 91 (lots of 5 m)*

**[1]**

> *Find the cost for 91 lots of \$48*

*91 × 48 = \$4368*

**\$4368** **[1]**

Sam has a rectangular pond, $ABCD$.

![q8a-058033-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/007-q8a-058033-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

i) Calculate $BC$.

$BC$ = ...............................m [3]

ii) He puts a fence around the edge of the pond. 
Calculate the length of the fence.

................................m [1]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Find the length of *$BC$* using Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$

$7^{2}+BC^{2}=12^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract *$7^{2}$* from both sides*

$BC^{2}=12^{2}-7^{2}$

> *Take the square root of both sides*

$BC=\sqrt{12^{2}-7^{2}}$

**[1]**

$BC=9.75m$ **[1]**

**Answers between 9.746 and 9.747 will be accepted**

ii) *The length of the fence will be the same as the perimeter of the rectangle* *Add up the lengths of all of the sides of the rectangle*

$7+7+9.75+9.75$

$33.5m$ **[1]**

**Answers between 33.492 and 33.494 or an answer of 33.49 will be accepted**
